en: Virgin coconut oil solidifies in cool Baguio City but melts into a liquid in the warmer climate of Manila.
Water in Tagaytay City boils at a lower temperature than in sea-level Manila because higher altitudes have lower atmospheric pressure.
Fermenting salted anchovies into fish sauce, or patis, in Guiguinto, Bulacan, is a chemical change producing new substances.
Slicing sweet mangoes from Guimaras into pieces for dessert is a physical change because the fruit's chemical composition remains unchanged.
Dissolving dark muscovado sugar from Negros Occidental into hot Barako coffee from Batangas creates a homogeneous liquid solution.
Mixing white sand from Boracay beaches with seawater creates a heterogeneous mixture that can be separated by filtration.
Lightweight pumice stones formed from Camiguin volcanoes float on the ocean because their overall density is less than water.
The dark magnetite sand found on the beaches of Ilocos Norte contains iron and is strongly attracted to magnets.
Copper extracted from the Philex mine in Benguet is drawn into wires because it is an excellent electrical conductor.
Crude oil pumped from the Galoc oil field in Palawan is highly viscous and flows much slower than water.
Abaca plant fibers harvested in Camarines Sur possess high tensile strength, making them ideal for weaving strong marine ropes.
Nipa palm leaves from the mangroves of Quezon province are woven into roofs because they are naturally water-resistant and flexible.
